summary: Optimizer circuit-breaker guidance for tenant batch/cache/quant experiments
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent elevated tail latency and occasional 502s after they applied a combined optimizer profile (aggressive batching + prefix KV caching + 4-bit quantization) to their production route. Impact: Several business-critical endpoints for MedAlign show 95th/99th latency spikes affecting real-time triage flows; customer requests a safe, tested way to cut optimizations without impacting throughput more than necessary. Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-owned node group) in prod-us-east serving two pinned model variants. Recent change: Applied optimizer profile v2026-03-09-agg which enabled aggressive batch grouping, enabled KV prefetch, and switched quantization profile to q4_main. Customer asks for: 1) immediate mitigation steps to stabilize latency and error rate; 2) a recommended circuit-breaker procedure (safe exit) that minimizes cold-cache penalties; 3) a checklist for future experiments to avoid similar disruption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's production route (medalign-triage-v1) and send representative traffic with 1-3 sentence prompts at 40 rps sustained.
2) Apply optimizer profile v2026-03-09-agg which sets batch_size: 48, max_batch_delay_ms: 50, kv_prefetch: enabled, quant_profile: q4_main aggressive packing.
3) Observe metrics on Console: per-route p95/p99 latency jumps after ~10 minutes and occasional 502/504 spikes.
4) Reproduce by toggling kv_prefetch on/off via customer config change and watching tail latency delta.
5) Re-run with traffic split: 10% to profile-on, 90% baseline and inspect per-split latency and error rates.

comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Desai (Support): Opened with priority P1 after customer reported production impact. Customer willing to accept short traffic reduction to enable safe rollback. Requested immediate mitigation steps and formalized circuit-breaker guidance.

2026-03-10 Ethan Miller (SRE): Investigating. Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching increased queueing under spikey seq-length distribution; KV prefetch caused additional memory pressure on dedicated GPU leading to kernel faults for large batches. Will correlate GPU memory OOM events and scheduler logs.

2026-03-11 MedAlign (Customer): Provided traffic profile and representative prompt set. Notes: the issue is intermittent, appears more often during clinical report uploads that include longer context.

2026-03-11 Ethan Miller (SRE): Ran canary with 90/10 traffic split. Observed p99 latency 3x higher for profile-on. Uploaded preliminary dashboard snapshots to ticket. Suggested immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch_delay_ms to 10ms, cap batch_size to 16, and temporarily disable kv_prefetch to allow graceful fallback while preserving q4_main for cost reasons.

2026-03-12 Priya Desai (Support): Customer executed suggested mitigation with Support guidance; p99 improved but throughput dropped ~12%. Customer requests a documented safe-exit procedure to fully remove the aggressive profile later and reintroduce optimizations incrementally.

2026-03-13 Ethan Miller (SRE): Drafted circuit-breaker playbook and runbook, attached as steps in investigation_notes and resolution. Recommended rolling traffic split and snapshot export of KV caches before full disable. Assigned follow-ups to onboarding and infra teams for per-tenant snapshot tooling.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Large batch sizes cause kernel scheduling contention on our dedicated pool GPUs; q4 packing increased compute density and increased end-to-end kernel latency leading to timeouts.
Hypothesis 2: KV prefetch interacts poorly with packed quantized weights and LRU eviction on tenant cache causing frequent cache churn and higher memory churn.
Metrics observed: spike in gpu_utilization and gpu_memory_free dips correlated with p99 latency peaks. Scheduler queue length rose to batch_size/2 during peaks.
Dashboards examined: per-tenant latency (Console), GPU telemetry (Prometheus), scheduler queues (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimizer/scheduler?orgId=1&from=now-1h)
Short tests: reducing batch_size to 16 reduced p99 by ~45% in canary; disabling kv_prefetch reduced 502s to baseline but increased average token cost by ~6%.

Risk assessment: Full immediate disable of optimizer profile will result in cold-kv-cache misses and a transient latency bump for first requests; long-term throughput is expected to settle within 10-30 minutes depending on traffic volume.
resolution: Mitigation taken (2026-03-11): Applied 'soft-fallback' profile for medalign-triage-v1: batch_size=16, max_batch_delay_ms=10, kv_prefetch=disabled, quant_profile=q4_main (unchanged). This stabilized tail latency and eliminated 502s. Noted throughput drop ~12%.
Step 1 - Snapshot: Export current optimizer profile and persist tenant KV cache snapshot via admin API snapshot/tenant/medalign before any full disable.
Step 2 - Canary: Create a 5-10% traffic split to a 'safe' profile (batch_size=8-16, kv_prefetch=off, quant_profile=q4_safe) for 30 minutes and monitor p95/p99 and error rate.
Step 3 - Ramp: If canary stable, increase split by doubling every 15 minutes while watching p99 and GPU memory trends; abort if p99 > threshold or errors rise > 1% of baseline.
Step 4 - Full switch: Once at 100%, keep monitoring for 1 hour to allow KV caches to warm gradually; run a background cache-prewarm job if available to reduce cold miss window.

Step 5 - Re-introduction: To re-enable optimizations later, run the inverse: canary enable one knob at a time (first quant_profile change or batch_size increase, then kv_prefetch) and observe for 2x the expected latency window.

Follow-ups assigned: Implement admin API to take atomic tenant optimizer snapshots (INT-404), add a per-tenant prewarm helper in the console (ENG-881), update runbooks with the above playbook (Confluence page link provided).
Outcome: Customer accepted the soft-fallback and requested the formal playbook. Ticket remains open until snapshot tooling delivery and runbook updates are completed.
